The choice of distillation method depends on volatility, boiling point differences, thermal stability, and mutual solubility with water.

Step 2: Analysis of List I entries
- Chloroform (b.p. \(334\text{ K}\)) and aniline (b.p. \(457\text{ K}\)) have a large boiling point difference of \(123\text{ K}\). Liquids that boil without decomposition and have sufficiently wide boiling point differences (\(>25\text{ K}\)) are cleanly separated by simple distillation.
- Crude oil contains complex mixtures of liquid hydrocarbons with closely spaced boiling points. When boiling point differences are small, separation is achieved using a fractionating column via fractional distillation.
- Glycerol has a very high boiling point (\(563\text{ K}\)) and decomposes at or below its normal boiling point. In the soap industry, it is separated from spent-lye by distillation under reduced pressure (vacuum distillation), enabling it to boil at a much lower temperature without thermal degradation.
- Aniline is practically immiscible with water, volatile in steam, and possesses a significant partial vapor pressure at \(373\text{ K}\). Aniline from an aniline-water mixture is separated using steam distillation, which distills the mixture at a total pressure equal to atmospheric pressure at a temperature below \(373\text{ K}\).

Step 3: Verification of Pairings
- Chloroform and aniline corresponds to simple distillation.
- Crude oil fractions corresponds to fractional distillation.
- Glycerol from spent-lye corresponds to distillation under reduced pressure.
- Aniline from an aniline-water mixture corresponds to steam distillation.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The correct matching sequence is A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ORGANIC_QUALITATIVE_ANALYSIS_MCQ_Q08 - Observations and products in Lassaignes elemental tests

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Qualitative Detection Test) List II (Observation / Reaction Product)
(A) Detection of nitrogen in Lassaigne's extract (I) Blood red colouration due to \([\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{SCN})]^{2+}\)
(B) Detection of sulphur using lead acetate (II) Prussian blue precipitate/colouration of \(\mathrm{Fe}_4[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6]_3\cdot x\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\)
(C) Detection of sulphur using sodium nitroprusside (III) Black precipitate of \(\mathrm{PbS}\)
(D) Simultaneous detection of nitrogen and sulphur (IV) Violet colouration due to \([\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_5\mathrm{NOS}]^{4-}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In Lassaigne's test, organic compounds are fused with metallic sodium to convert covalently bonded heteroatoms (nitrogen, sulphur, halogens) into water-soluble ionic salts: \(\mathrm{NaCN}\), \(\mathrm{Na_2S}\), and \(\mathrm{NaSCN}\), which are subsequently identified via characteristic precipitation or complexation reactions.

Step 2: Analysis of List I entries
- When nitrogen alone is present, sodium fusion produces \(\mathrm{NaCN}\). Boiling with iron(II) sulphate (\(\mathrm{FeSO_4}\)) forms sodium hexacyanoferrate(II). Upon acidification with concentrated sulphuric acid, \(\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}\) is oxidised to \(\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}\), which reacts with hexacyanoferrate(II) to yield a Prussian blue complex, iron(III) hexacyanoferrate(II), \(\mathrm{Fe_4[Fe(CN)_6]_3\cdot xH_2O}\).
- When sulphur is present, sodium fusion produces \(\mathrm{Na_2S}\). Acidifying the extract with acetic acid followed by the addition of lead acetate solution produces a black precipitate of lead sulphide, \(\mathrm{PbS}\).
- Sulphur in the sodium fusion extract (\(\mathrm{Na_2S}\)) also reacts with freshly prepared aqueous sodium nitroprusside, \(\mathrm{Na_2[Fe(CN)_5NO]}\), yielding an intense violet colouration due to the formation of the complex ion \([\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_5\mathrm{NOS}]^{4-}\).
- When both nitrogen and sulphur are simultaneously present and sodium is not in large excess, sodium thiocyanate (\(\mathrm{NaSCN}\)) is formed. Upon adding \(\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}\) ions (from \(\mathrm{FeCl_3}\)), a characteristic blood red colouration appears due to the formation of \([\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{SCN})]^{2+}\) (ferric thiocyanate).

Step 3: Verification of Pairings
- Detection of nitrogen in Lassaigne's extract corresponds to Prussian blue precipitate/colouration of \(\mathrm{Fe}_4[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6]_3\cdot x\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\).
- Detection of sulphur using lead acetate corresponds to black precipitate of \(\mathrm{PbS}\).
- Detection of sulphur using sodium nitroprusside corresponds to violet colouration due to \([\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_5\mathrm{NOS}]^{4-}\).
- Simultaneous detection of nitrogen and sulphur corresponds to blood red colouration due to \([\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{SCN})]^{2+}\).

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The correct matching sequence is A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ORGANIC_QUANTITATIVE_ANALYSIS_MCQ_Q09 - Chemical principles of quantitative estimation methods

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Quantitative Method) List II (Working Chemical Principle)
(A) Dumas method for nitrogen (I) Digestion with concentrated \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\) to form \((\mathrm{NH}_4)_2\mathrm{SO}_4\), followed by distillation of \(\mathrm{NH}_3\) into standard acid
(B) Kjeldahl's method for nitrogen (II) Combustion with \(\mathrm{CuO}\) in a \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) atmosphere, reduction of nitrogen oxides, and collecting \(\mathrm{N_2}\) gas over aqueous \(\mathrm{KOH}\)
(C) Carius method for halogens (III) Heating with fuming \(\mathrm{HNO}_3\) and \(\mathrm{BaCl}_2\) in a sealed tube to precipitate and weigh \(\mathrm{BaSO}_4\)
(D) Carius method for sulphur (IV) Heating with fuming \(\mathrm{HNO}_3\) in the presence of \(\mathrm{AgNO}_3\) in a sealed tube to weigh \(\mathrm{AgX}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Quantitative elemental analysis involves stoichiometric conversion of elements present in organic compounds into measurable elemental gases, insoluble precipitates, or standard titratable solutions.

Step 2: Analysis of List I entries
- In Dumas method, a known mass of the nitrogenous compound is heated with copper(II) oxide in an atmosphere of \(\mathrm{CO_2}\). Any oxides of nitrogen formed are passed over a heated copper spiral to reduce them to elemental nitrogen. The gaseous mixture is transferred into a nitrometer containing concentrated \(\mathrm{KOH}\) solution, which absorbs \(\mathrm{CO_2}\), allowing the dry volume of \(\mathrm{N_2}\) gas to be measured.
- In Kjeldahl's method, the compound is digested with concentrated \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\) (in the presence of \(\mathrm{CuSO_4}\) catalyst and \(\mathrm{K_2SO_4}\) to raise the boiling point). Nitrogen is quantitatively converted to ammonium sulphate, \((\mathrm{NH_4})_2\mathrm{SO_4}\). Boiling the digested mixture with excess \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) releases ammonia gas (\(\mathrm{NH_3}\)), which is absorbed in a known excess volume of standard acid and determined by back-titration.
- In the Carius method for halogens, the compound is heated with fuming nitric acid (\(\mathrm{HNO_3}\)) in the presence of silver nitrate (\(\mathrm{AgNO_3}\)) inside a sealed heavy-walled glass Carius tube. The halogen is precipitated as silver halide (\(\mathrm{AgX}\)), which is filtered, washed, dried, and weighed.
- In the Carius method for sulphur, the organic compound is heated with fuming \(\mathrm{HNO_3}\) in a sealed Carius tube, oxidising sulphur to sulphuric acid. Barium chloride solution (\(\mathrm{BaCl_2}\)) is added to precipitate barium sulphate (\(\mathrm{BaSO_4}\)), which is washed, ignited, and weighed.

Step 3: Verification of Pairings
- Dumas method for nitrogen corresponds to combustion with \(\mathrm{CuO}\) in a \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) atmosphere, reduction of nitrogen oxides, and collecting \(\mathrm{N_2}\) gas over aqueous \(\mathrm{KOH}\).
- Kjeldahl's method for nitrogen corresponds to digestion with concentrated \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\) to form \((\mathrm{NH}_4)_2\mathrm{SO}_4\), followed by distillation of \(\mathrm{NH}_3\) into standard acid.
- Carius method for halogens corresponds to heating with fuming \(\mathrm{HNO}_3\) in the presence of \(\mathrm{AgNO}_3\) in a sealed tube to weigh \(\mathrm{AgX}\).
- Carius method for sulphur corresponds to heating with fuming \(\mathrm{HNO}_3\) and \(\mathrm{BaCl}_2\) in a sealed tube to precipitate and weigh \(\mathrm{BaSO}_4\).

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The correct matching sequence is A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ORGANIC_REAGENTS_ANALYSIS_MCQ_Q10 - Chemical reagents and their specific analytical detection functions

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Reagent / Absorbing Agent) List II (Specific Role / Analytical Detection)
(A) Ninhydrin spray reagent (I) Absorption of acidic \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) gas during quantitative carbon estimation or Dumas method
(B) Anhydrous copper(II) sulphate (II) Visualisation of colourless amino acid spots on thin layer or paper chromatograms
(C) Ammonium molybdate in boiling \(\mathrm{HNO_3}\) (III) Qualitative detection of water (hydrogen) formed during combustion by turning blue
(D) Concentrated potassium hydroxide solution (IV) Qualitative detection of phosphorus by formation of a canary yellow precipitate

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Qualitative, quantitative, and chromatographic analyses rely on specific chemical reagents and selective absorbents that produce unambiguous colour changes, precipitates, or chemical absorptions.

Step 2: Analysis of List I entries
- Ninhydrin spray solution is a specialised developing/visualising reagent used in thin-layer and paper chromatography to detect colourless amino acids and proteins, yielding a characteristic purple/violet Ruhemann's purple product upon reaction.
- Anhydrous copper(II) sulphate (\(\mathrm{CuSO_4}\)) is a white hygroscopic powder used in the Liebig combustion tube apparatus to detect water vapour generated from the oxidation of hydrogen present in the organic compound. As it hydrates to form \(\mathrm{CuSO_4\cdot 5H_2O}\), its colour distinctly changes from white to blue.
- Ammonium molybdate reagent in the presence of concentrated nitric acid is used to detect phosphorus. When the sodium peroxide fusion product (\(\mathrm{Na_3PO_4}\)) is boiled with nitric acid and treated with ammonium molybdate, \(\mathrm{(NH_4)_2MoO_4}\), it yields a characteristic canary yellow precipitate of ammonium phosphomolybdate, \(\mathrm{(NH_4)_3PO_4\cdot 12MoO_3}\).
- Concentrated aqueous potassium hydroxide solution (\(\mathrm{KOH}\)) is strongly alkaline and is specifically employed in Dumas nitrometers and Liebig combustion bulb sets to selectively absorb acidic carbon dioxide (\(\mathrm{CO_2}\)) gas according to \(2\mathrm{KOH} + \mathrm{CO_2} \rightarrow \mathrm{K_2CO_3} + \mathrm{H_2O}\).

Step 3: Verification of Pairings
- Ninhydrin spray reagent corresponds to visualisation of colourless amino acid spots on thin layer or paper chromatograms.
- Anhydrous copper(II) sulphate corresponds to qualitative detection of water (hydrogen) formed during combustion by turning blue.
- Ammonium molybdate in boiling \(\mathrm{HNO_3}\) corresponds to qualitative detection of phosphorus by formation of a canary yellow precipitate.
- Concentrated potassium hydroxide solution corresponds to absorption of acidic \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) gas during quantitative carbon estimation or Dumas method.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The correct matching sequence is A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_NUM_Q01 - Total number of sigma bonds in butenyne

questiontext.text: Calculate the total number of \(\sigma\) (sigma) bonds present in a molecule of but-1-en-3-yne, \(\mathrm{HC\equiv C-CH=CH_2}\).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given molecule: but-1-en-3-yne with condensed formula \(\mathrm{HC\equiv C-CH=CH_2}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
In covalent bonding, a single bond consists of one \(\sigma\) bond; a double bond consists of one \(\sigma\) bond and one \(\pi\) bond; a triple bond consists of one \(\sigma\) bond and two \(\pi\) bonds. Every carbon-hydrogen (\(\mathrm{C-H}\)) bond is a single \(\sigma\) bond.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Total \(\sigma\) bonds = \(\sum \sigma_{\mathrm{C-H}} + \sum \sigma_{\mathrm{C-C}}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Counting individual bonds: - Number of \(\mathrm{C-H}\) \(\sigma\) bonds: one at \(\mathrm{C1}\), one at \(\mathrm{C3}\), and two at \(\mathrm{C4}\), giving \(1 + 1 + 2 = 4\) \(\sigma_{\mathrm{C-H}}\) bonds. - Number of \(\mathrm{C-C}\) \(\sigma\) bonds: one \(\sigma\) bond in the triple bond \(\mathrm{C1\equiv C2}\), one \(\sigma\) bond in the single bond \(\mathrm{C2-C3}\), and one \(\sigma\) bond in the double bond \(\mathrm{C3=C4}\), giving \(1 + 1 + 1 = 3\) \(\sigma_{\mathrm{C-C}}\) bonds. - Total number of \(\sigma\) bonds = \(4 + 3 = 7\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking the total atoms: in an acyclic molecule with \(n\) atoms, total \(\sigma\) bonds equal \(n - 1\). Here the formula is \(\mathrm{C_4H_4}\), total atoms = 8. Thus, \(\sigma\) bonds = \(8 - 1 = 7\). The value is verified. The final answer is 7.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_NUM_Q02 - Retardation factor calculation in thin layer chromatography

questiontext.text: In a thin layer chromatography (TLC) experiment, a compound moves a distance of \(3.6\text{ cm}\) from the baseline while the solvent front moves \(9.0\text{ cm}\) from the baseline. Calculate the retardation factor (\(R_f\) value) of the compound.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Distance moved by the substance from baseline, \(x = 3.6\text{ cm}\); distance moved by the solvent front from baseline, \(y = 9.0\text{ cm}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
The retardation factor \(R_f\) is a dimensionless ratio defined under uniform chromatographic conditions.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
\(R_f = \dfrac{\text{Distance moved by the substance from baseline } (x)}{\text{Distance moved by the solvent from baseline } (y)}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substituting the given values into the formula: \[R_f = \frac{3.6\text{ cm}}{9.0\text{ cm}} = 0.40\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Since the solute travels less than the solvent front, \(R_f\) must be between 0 and 1. The calculated value \(0.40\) lies within this range. The final answer is 0.4.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_NUM_Q03 - Total number of pi bonds in hexadienyne

questiontext.text: Determine the total number of \(\pi\) (pi) bonds present in a molecule of hexa-1,3-dien-5-yne, \(\mathrm{CH\equiv C-CH=CH-CH=CH_2}\).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given molecule: hexa-1,3-dien-5-yne with condensed structural formula \(\mathrm{CH\equiv C-CH=CH-CH=CH_2}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
A carbon-carbon single bond contains zero \(\pi\) bonds; a carbon-carbon double bond (\(\mathrm{C=C}\)) contains one \(\sigma\) and one \(\pi\) bond; a carbon-carbon triple bond (\(\mathrm{C\equiv C}\)) contains one \(\sigma\) and two \(\pi\) bonds.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Total \(\pi\) bonds = \(\sum \pi_{\mathrm{C=C}} + \sum \pi_{\mathrm{C\equiv C}}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Identifying the multiple bonds in the structure: - There is one triple bond at position 5: \(\mathrm{C5\equiv C6}\), which contributes \(2\) \(\pi\) bonds. - There are two double bonds at positions 1 and 3: \(\mathrm{C1=C2}\) and \(\mathrm{C3=C4}\), each contributing \(1\) \(\pi\) bond. - Total number of \(\pi\) bonds = \(2 + 1 + 1 = 4\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Verifying by checking the degree of unsaturation (hydrogen deficiency index) for \(\mathrm{C_6H_6}\): for an alkane with 6 carbons, maximum hydrogens = \(2 \times 6 + 2 = 14\). Here, hydrogens = 6. Unsaturation index = \((14 - 6)/2 = 4\). Since the molecule is acyclic, all 4 units of unsaturation are \(\pi\) bonds. The final answer is 4.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_NUM_Q04 - Number of hyperconjugating hydrogens in carbocation

questiontext.text: Find the number of \(\alpha\)-hydrogen atoms available for hyperconjugative stabilization in the *tert*-butyl carbocation, \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_3C^+}\).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given species: *tert*-butyl cation, \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_3C^+}\), in which three methyl groups are directly attached to the positively charged central carbon.

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
Hyperconjugation involves the delocalisation of \(\sigma\) electrons of \(\mathrm{C-H}\) bonds on carbon atoms directly adjacent (\(\alpha\)-position) to the positively charged carbon containing an empty \(2p\) orbital.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Total hyperconjugating hydrogens = \(\sum (\text{hydrogens on each attached } \alpha\text{-carbon})\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
The central carbon \(\mathrm{C^+}\) is bonded to three equivalent methyl (\(-\mathrm{CH_3}\)) groups. Each methyl group contains \(3\) \(\mathrm{C-H}\) bonds attached to the \(\alpha\)-carbon. Thus, total number of \(\alpha\)-hydrogen atoms = \(3 \times 3 = 9\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Each of the 9 \(\mathrm{C-H}\) bonds can independently enter into no-bond resonance with the vacant \(2p\) orbital, explaining the high stability of the tertiary carbocation. The final answer is 9.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_NUM_Q05 - Percentage of carbon in organic compound combustion

questiontext.text: During the quantitative estimation of carbon by Liebig's method, complete combustion of \(0.30\text{ g}\) of an organic compound produced \(0.44\text{ g}\) of carbon dioxide. Calculate the mass percentage of carbon in the compound.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of organic compound taken, \(m = 0.30\text{ g}\); mass of carbon dioxide (\(\mathrm{CO_2}\)) produced, \(m_2 = 0.44\text{ g}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
All carbon present in the organic compound is quantitatively oxidised to \(\mathrm{CO_2}\). Molar mass of \(\mathrm{CO_2} = 12 + 2 \times 16 = 44\text{ g mol}^{-1}\); atomic mass of carbon = \(12\text{ g mol}^{-1}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Percentage of carbon = \(\dfrac{12 \times m_2 \times 100}{44 \times m}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the measured masses into the expression: \[\text{Percentage of carbon} = \frac{12 \times 0.44\text{ g} \times 100}{44 \times 0.30\text{ g}}\] Simplify the numerator and denominator: \[\frac{12 \times 0.44}{44} = \frac{12 \times 0.01} = 0.12\text{ g of carbon}\] \[\text{Percentage of carbon} = \frac{0.12}{0.30} \times 100 = 40.0\%\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The calculated percentage \(40.0\%\) is positive and less than 100%, which is physically consistent. The final answer is 40.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_NUM_Q06 - Percentage of hydrogen from combustion water mass

questiontext.text: In the estimation of hydrogen in an organic compound, complete combustion of \(0.20\text{ g}\) of the substance yielded \(0.18\text{ g}\) of water. Calculate the percentage of hydrogen in the compound.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of organic compound, \(m = 0.20\text{ g}\); mass of water (\(\mathrm{H_2O}\)) collected in the calcium chloride tube, \(m_1 = 0.18\text{ g}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
All hydrogen in the organic compound is converted to water. Molar mass of \(\mathrm{H_2O} = 2 \times 1 + 16 = 18\text{ g mol}^{-1}\); mass of two hydrogen atoms in one mole of water = \(2\text{ g mol}^{-1}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Percentage of hydrogen = \(\dfrac{2 \times m_1 \times 100}{18 \times m}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substituting the values into the formula: \[\text{Percentage of hydrogen} = \frac{2 \times 0.18\text{ g} \times 100}{18 \times 0.20\text{ g}}\] Evaluating intermediate steps: \[\frac{2 \times 0.18}{18} = 0.02\text{ g of hydrogen}\] \[\text{Percentage of hydrogen} = \frac{0.02}{0.20} \times 100 = 10.0\%\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking the result: \(0.02\text{ g}\) of hydrogen out of \(0.20\text{ g}\) compound is exactly \(1/10\) of the total mass, giving \(10.0\%\). The final answer is 10.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_NUM_Q07 - Percentage of bromine by Carius method estimation

questiontext.text: In Carius method of estimation of halogen, \(0.25\text{ g}\) of an organic bromo compound gave \(0.188\text{ g}\) of silver bromide (\(\mathrm{AgBr}\)). Calculate the percentage of bromine in the compound. (Take atomic masses: \(\mathrm{Ag} = 108\text{ u}\), \(\mathrm{Br} = 80\text{ u}\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of organic compound, \(m = 0.25\text{ g}\); mass of silver bromide (\(\mathrm{AgBr}\)) formed, \(m_1 = 0.188\text{ g}\); atomic masses: \(\mathrm{Ag} = 108\text{ g mol}^{-1}\), \(\mathrm{Br} = 80\text{ g mol}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
Molar mass of \(\mathrm{AgBr} = 108 + 80 = 188\text{ g mol}^{-1}\). One mole of \(\mathrm{AgBr}\) (\(188\text{ g}\)) contains one mole of bromine atoms (\(80\text{ g}\)).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Percentage of bromine = \(\dfrac{80 \times m_1 \times 100}{188 \times m}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substituting the given data: \[\text{Percentage of bromine} = \frac{80 \times 0.188\text{ g} \times 100}{188 \times 0.25\text{ g}}\] Notice that \(\dfrac{0.188}{188} = 0.001\text{ mol}\). Mass of bromine in precipitate = \(80 \times 0.001\text{ g} = 0.08\text{ g}\). \[\text{Percentage of bromine} = \frac{0.08}{0.25} \times 100 = 32.0\%\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking the calculation: \(0.08 / 0.25 = 8/25 = 32/100 = 32.0\%\). Units and magnitude are verified. The final answer is 32.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_NUM_Q08 - Percentage of sulphur in Carius method estimation

questiontext.text: In the estimation of sulphur by Carius method, \(0.16\text{ g}\) of an organic compound afforded \(0.233\text{ g}\) of barium sulphate (\(\mathrm{BaSO_4}\)). Calculate the percentage of sulphur in the given compound. (Take molar mass of \(\mathrm{BaSO_4} = 233\text{ g mol}^{-1}\), atomic mass of \(\mathrm{S} = 32\text{ u}\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of organic compound taken, \(m = 0.16\text{ g}\); mass of \(\mathrm{BaSO_4}\) formed, \(m_1 = 0.233\text{ g}\); molar mass of \(\mathrm{BaSO_4} = 233\text{ g mol}^{-1}\); atomic mass of \(\mathrm{S} = 32\text{ g mol}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
Sulphur present in the organic compound is oxidised to sulphuric acid and precipitated quantitatively as \(\mathrm{BaSO_4}\). Each mole of \(\mathrm{BaSO_4}\) contains one mole of sulphur.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Percentage of sulphur = \(\dfrac{32 \times m_1 \times 100}{233 \times m}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substituting the given values: \[\text{Percentage of sulphur} = \frac{32 \times 0.233\text{ g} \times 100}{233 \times 0.16\text{ g}}\] Calculate the mole of \(\mathrm{BaSO_4}\): \[\frac{0.233}{233} = 0.001\text{ mol}\] Mass of sulphur present = \(32 \times 0.001 = 0.032\text{ g}\). \[\text{Percentage of sulphur} = \frac{0.032\text{ g}}{0.16\text{ g}} \times 100 = 20.0\%\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking ratio: \(0.032 / 0.16 = 32 / 160 = 0.20 = 20.0\%\). The percentage is physically plausible. The final answer is 20.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_NUM_Q09 - Percentage of chlorine by Carius tube estimation

questiontext.text: In a Carius estimation of halogen, \(0.20\text{ g}\) of an organic chloro compound gave \(0.287\text{ g}\) of silver chloride (\(\mathrm{AgCl}\)). Find the percentage of chlorine present in the compound. (Take atomic masses: \(\mathrm{Ag} = 108\text{ u}\), \(\mathrm{Cl} = 35.5\text{ u}\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of organic compound, \(m = 0.20\text{ g}\); mass of \(\mathrm{AgCl}\) precipitate, \(m_1 = 0.287\text{ g}\); atomic masses: \(\mathrm{Ag} = 108\text{ g mol}^{-1}\), \(\mathrm{Cl} = 35.5\text{ g mol}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
Molar mass of \(\mathrm{AgCl} = 108 + 35.5 = 143.5\text{ g mol}^{-1}\). In \(143.5\text{ g}\) of \(\mathrm{AgCl}\), there are \(35.5\text{ g}\) of chlorine.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Percentage of chlorine = \(\dfrac{35.5 \times m_1 \times 100}{143.5 \times m}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substituting the values into the formula: \[\text{Percentage of chlorine} = \frac{35.5 \times 0.287\text{ g} \times 100}{143.5 \times 0.20\text{ g}}\] Evaluate \(\dfrac{0.287}{143.5} = 0.002\text{ mol}\). Mass of chlorine = \(35.5 \times 0.002 = 0.071\text{ g}\). \[\text{Percentage of chlorine} = \frac{0.071}{0.20} \times 100 = 35.5\%\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Verification: \(0.071 / 0.20 = 71 / 200 = 35.5\%\). Units and calculation are verified. The final answer is 35.5.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_NUM_Q10 - Percentage of nitrogen in organic Kjeldahl analysis

questiontext.text: During estimation of nitrogen in an organic compound by Kjeldahl's method, the ammonia evolved from \(0.35\text{ g}\) of the compound neutralized \(10\text{ mL}\) of \(0.5\text{ M } \mathrm{H_2SO_4}\). Calculate the percentage of nitrogen in the compound.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of organic compound taken, \(m = 0.35\text{ g}\); volume of sulphuric acid neutralized, \(V = 10\text{ mL}\); molarity of sulphuric acid, \(M = 0.5\text{ M}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
The reaction between ammonia and sulphuric acid is: \[2\mathrm{NH_3} + \mathrm{H_2SO_4} \longrightarrow (\mathrm{NH_4})_2\mathrm{SO_4}\] Hence, \(1\text{ mol of } \mathrm{H_2SO_4} \equiv 2\text{ mol of } \mathrm{NH_3} \equiv 2\text{ mol of } \mathrm{N} = 28\text{ g of nitrogen}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Percentage of nitrogen = \(\dfrac{1.4 \times M \times 2 \times V}{m}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substituting the parameters: \[\text{Moles of } \mathrm{H_2SO_4} \text{ neutralized} = \frac{10 \times 0.5}{1000} = 0.005\text{ mol}\] \[\text{Moles of } \mathrm{NH_3} = 2 \times 0.005 = 0.010\text{ mol}\] \[\text{Mass of nitrogen} = 0.010\text{ mol} \times 14\text{ g mol}^{-1} = 0.14\text{ g}\] \[\text{Percentage of nitrogen} = \frac{0.14\text{ g}}{0.35\text{ g}} \times 100 = 40.0\%\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Using the shortcut formula: \(\dfrac{1.4 \times 0.5 \times 2 \times 10}{0.35} = \dfrac{14}{0.35} = 40.0\%\). Both methods agree. The final answer is 40.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_NUM_Q11 - Count of sp2 hybridized carbons in hydrocarbon

questiontext.text: Determine the number of \(sp^2\) hybridised carbon atoms in a molecule of hepta-1,3-dien-5-yne, \(\mathrm{CH_2=CH-CH=CH-C\equiv C-CH_3}\).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given compound: hepta-1,3-dien-5-yne with condensed structure \(\mathrm{\overset{1}{C}H_2=\overset{2}{C}H-\overset{3}{C}H=\overset{4}{C}H-\overset{5}{C}\equiv \overset{6}{C}-\overset{7}{C}H_3}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
The state of hybridisation of each carbon atom is determined by the number of \(\sigma\) bonds (steric number) it forms: - Carbon forming 4 \(\sigma\) bonds is \(sp^3\) hybridised. - Carbon forming 3 \(\sigma\) bonds (one double bond and two single bonds) is \(sp^2\) hybridised. - Carbon forming 2 \(\sigma\) bonds (one triple bond and one single bond, or two double bonds) is \(sp\) hybridised.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Evaluate the hybridisation state of each of the 7 carbon atoms systematically.

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Analysing each carbon atom along the chain: - \(\mathrm{C1}\): forms two \(\mathrm{C-H}\) \(\sigma\) bonds and one \(\mathrm{C-C}\) \(\sigma\) bond (total 3 \(\sigma\) bonds) \(\longrightarrow sp^2\). - \(\mathrm{C2}\): forms one \(\mathrm{C-H}\) \(\sigma\) bond and two \(\mathrm{C-C}\) \(\sigma\) bonds (total 3 \(\sigma\) bonds) \(\longrightarrow sp^2\). - \(\mathrm{C3}\): forms one \(\mathrm{C-H}\) \(\sigma\) bond and two \(\mathrm{C-C}\) \(\sigma\) bonds (total 3 \(\sigma\) bonds) \(\longrightarrow sp^2\). - \(\mathrm{C4}\): forms one \(\mathrm{C-H}\) \(\sigma\) bond and two \(\mathrm{C-C}\) \(\sigma\) bonds (total 3 \(\sigma\) bonds) \(\longrightarrow sp^2\). - \(\mathrm{C5}\): forms one \(\mathrm{C-C}\) single \(\sigma\) bond and one \(\mathrm{C\equiv C}\) \(\sigma\) bond (total 2 \(\sigma\) bonds) \(\longrightarrow sp\). - \(\mathrm{C6}\): forms one \(\mathrm{C\equiv C}\) \(\sigma\) bond and one \(\mathrm{C-C}\) single \(\sigma\) bond (total 2 \(\sigma\) bonds) \(\longrightarrow sp\). - \(\mathrm{C7}\): forms one \(\mathrm{C-C}\) \(\sigma\) bond and three \(\mathrm{C-H}\) \(\sigma\) bonds (total 4 \(\sigma\) bonds) \(\longrightarrow sp^3\). Thus, carbon atoms 1, 2, 3, and 4 are \(sp^2\) hybridised, giving a total of 4.

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Total carbons = 7. Breakdown: 4 \(sp^2\) + 2 \(sp\) + 1 \(sp^3\) = 7. All atoms are accounted for. The final answer is 4.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_NUM_Q12 - Number of structural chain isomers of pentane

questiontext.text: How many acyclic structural chain isomers are possible for an alkane having the molecular formula \(\mathrm{C_5H_{12}}\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given molecular formula of saturated acyclic alkane: \(\mathrm{C_5H_{12}}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
Chain isomers are compounds having the same molecular formula but different carbon skeletons (arrangements of the carbon backbone).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Construct all unique non-cyclic carbon skeleton connectivity networks of 5 carbon atoms.

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Identifying the distinct carbon chain arrangements: 1. Unbranched 5-carbon continuous chain: \(\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-CH_2-CH_3}\) (pentane or *n*-pentane). 2. 4-carbon chain with a single one-carbon branch at \(\mathrm{C2}\): \(\mathrm{CH_3-CH(CH_3)-CH_2-CH_3}\) (2-methylbutane or isopentane). 3. 3-carbon chain with two one-carbon branches at \(\mathrm{C2}\): \(\mathrm{CH_3-C(CH_3)_2-CH_3}\) (2,2-dimethylpropane or neopentane). Any other placement is structurally identical due to symmetry. Thus, exactly 3 chain isomers exist.

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking IUPAC names: pentane, 2-methylbutane, and 2,2-dimethylpropane are distinct and complete the set of constitutional isomers for \(\mathrm{C_5H_{12}}\). The final answer is 3.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_NUM_Q13 - Percentage of phosphorus in phosphomolybdate precipitation

questiontext.text: In the quantitative analysis of phosphorus, \(0.10\text{ g}\) of an organic compound was heated with fuming nitric acid and then treated with ammonium molybdate. The mass of ammonium phosphomolybdate, \(\mathrm{(NH_4)_3PO_4\cdot 12MoO_3}\), precipitated was \(0.3754\text{ g}\). Calculate the percentage of phosphorus in the compound. (Take molar mass of \(\mathrm{(NH_4)_3PO_4\cdot 12MoO_3} = 1877\text{ g mol}^{-1}\), atomic mass of \(\mathrm{P} = 31\text{ u}\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of organic compound, \(m = 0.10\text{ g}\); mass of ammonium phosphomolybdate precipitate, \(m_1 = 0.3754\text{ g}\); molar mass of precipitate = \(1877\text{ g mol}^{-1}\); atomic mass of phosphorus = \(31\text{ g mol}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
All phosphorus in the organic compound is converted to phosphoric acid and precipitated as \(\mathrm{(NH_4)_3PO_4\cdot 12MoO_3}\). Each mole of precipitate contains exactly one mole of phosphorus.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Percentage of phosphorus = \(\dfrac{31 \times m_1 \times 100}{1877 \times m}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substituting the measured data into the formula: \[\text{Percentage of phosphorus} = \frac{31 \times 0.3754\text{ g} \times 100}{1877 \times 0.10\text{ g}}\] Evaluate \(\dfrac{0.3754}{1877}\): \[\frac{0.3754}{1877} = 0.0002\text{ mol}\] Mass of phosphorus = \(31 \times 0.0002 = 0.0062\text{ g}\). \[\text{Percentage of phosphorus} = \frac{0.0062\text{ g}}{0.10\text{ g}} \times 100 = 6.2\%\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Check: \(0.0062 / 0.10 = 0.062 = 6.2\%\). Units are correct and value is physically reasonable. The final answer is 6.2.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_NUM_Q14 - Number of isomeric aliphatic alcohols of propanol

questiontext.text: How many constitutional (position) isomers of aliphatic alcohols can be represented by the molecular formula \(\mathrm{C_3H_8O}\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given molecular formula: \(\mathrm{C_3H_8O}\), restricted to aliphatic alcohols (containing the \(-\mathrm{OH}\) functional group).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
In saturated monohydric alcohols of formula \(\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+2}O}\), isomerism arises from differing positions of the hydroxyl group on the carbon skeleton.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
A 3-carbon skeleton allows attachment of the \(-\mathrm{OH}\) group at distinct non-equivalent positions.

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Examining the propane backbone \(\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-CH_3}\): 1. Attachment of \(-\mathrm{OH}\) at a terminal carbon (\(\mathrm{C1}\)): \(\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-OH}\) (propan-1-ol). 2. Attachment of \(-\mathrm{OH}\) at the middle secondary carbon (\(\mathrm{C2}\)): \(\mathrm{CH_3-CH(OH)-CH_3}\) (propan-2-ol). Attachment at \(\mathrm{C3}\) is chemically identical to \(\mathrm{C1}\) due to symmetry. Hence, exactly 2 alcohol isomers are possible.

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Both propan-1-ol and propan-2-ol have molecular formula \(\mathrm{C_3H_8O}\) and represent the complete set of isomeric alcohols. The final answer is 2.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_NUM_Q15 - Percentage of nitrogen via Kjeldahl back titration

questiontext.text: A sample of \(0.50\text{ g}\) of an organic compound was treated according to Kjeldahl's method. The ammonia evolved was absorbed in \(50\text{ mL}\) of \(0.5\text{ M } \mathrm{H_2SO_4}\). The residual acid required \(60\text{ mL}\) of \(0.5\text{ M } \mathrm{NaOH}\) solution for complete neutralisation. Calculate the percentage of nitrogen in the compound.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of organic compound, \(m = 0.50\text{ g}\); initial volume of \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\), \(V = 50\text{ mL}\); molarity of acid, \(M = 0.5\text{ M}\); volume of \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) used for back-titration, \(V_1 = 60\text{ mL}\); molarity of \(\mathrm{NaOH} = 0.5\text{ M}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
Ammonia reacts with sulphuric acid according to: \[2\mathrm{NH_3} + \mathrm{H_2SO_4} \\longrightarrow (\mathrm{NH_4})_2\mathrm{SO_4}\] Unreacted sulphuric acid is neutralised by sodium hydroxide: \[\mathrm{H_2SO_4} + 2\mathrm{NaOH} \\longrightarrow \mathrm{Na_2SO_4} + 2\mathrm{H_2O}\] Thus, \(2\text{ moles of } \mathrm{NaOH} \equiv 1\text{ mole of } \mathrm{H_2SO_4}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Volume of \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\) of molarity \(M\) unused = \(V - \dfrac{V_1}{2}\). Volume of \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\) reacted with \(\mathrm{NH_3} = V - \left(V - \dfrac{V_1}{2}\right) = \text{initial} - \text{unused}\). Percentage of nitrogen = \(\dfrac{1.4 \times M \times 2 \left(V - \dfrac{V_1}{2}\right)}{m}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculating step-by-step: - Initial millimoles of \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4} = 50\text{ mL} \times 0.5\text{ M} = 25.0\text{ mmol}\). - Millimoles of \(\mathrm{NaOH} = 60\text{ mL} \times 0.5\text{ M} = 30.0\text{ mmol}\). - Unreacted millimoles of \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4} = \dfrac{30.0}{2} = 15.0\text{ mmol}\). - Millimoles of \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\) consumed by \(\mathrm{NH_3} = 25.0 - 15.0 = 10.0\text{ mmol}\). - Millimoles of \(\mathrm{NH_3}\) evolved = \(2 \times 10.0 = 20.0\text{ mmol}\). - Mass of nitrogen = \(20.0\text{ mmol} \times 10^{-3}\text{ mol mmol}^{-1} \times 14\text{ g mol}^{-1} = 0.28\text{ g}\). - Percentage of nitrogen = \(\dfrac{0.28\text{ g}}{0.50\text{ g}} \times 100 = 56.0\%\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking formula directly: \(V - V_1/2 = 50 - 30 = 20\text{ mL}\). \(\text{Percentage of N} = \dfrac{1.4 \times 0.5 \times 2 \times 20}{0.50} = \dfrac{28}{0.50} = 56.0\%\). Both methods yield identical results. The final answer is 56.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_NUM_Q16 - Nitrogen estimation by Dumas method aqueous tension

questiontext.text: In Dumas' method for estimation of nitrogen, \(0.30\text{ g}\) of an organic compound gave \(50.0\text{ mL}\) of nitrogen gas collected over aqueous \(\mathrm{KOH}\) at \(300\text{ K}\) and \(715\text{ mm Hg}\) pressure. If the aqueous tension at \(300\text{ K}\) is \(15\text{ mm Hg}\), calculate the percentage of nitrogen in the compound. (Give answer to two decimal places).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of organic compound, \(m = 0.30\text{ g}\); volume of nitrogen collected, \(V_1 = 50.0\text{ mL}\); temperature, \(T_1 = 300\text{ K}\); barometric pressure = \(715\text{ mm Hg}\); aqueous tension = \(15\text{ mm Hg}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
The pressure of dry nitrogen gas is obtained by subtracting the aqueous tension of water from the barometric pressure. Standard temperature is \(T_0 = 273\text{ K}\) and standard pressure is \(P_0 = 760\text{ mm Hg}\). Under STP, \(22400\text{ mL}\) of \(\mathrm{N_2}\) weighs \(28\text{ g}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Actual pressure of dry nitrogen: \(p_1 = \text{Atmospheric pressure} - \text{Aqueous tension}\). Volume of dry nitrogen at STP: \(V = \dfrac{p_1 \times V_1 \times 273}{760 \times T_1}\). Percentage of nitrogen: \(\text{Percentage of N} = \dfrac{28 \times V \times 100}{22400 \times m}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Executing calculations step by step: 1. \(p_1 = 715 - 15 = 700\text{ mm Hg}\). 2. \(V = \dfrac{700 \times 50.0 \times 273}{760 \times 300} = \dfrac{9555000}{228000} \approx 41.908\text{ mL}\). 3. Mass of \(41.908\text{ mL}\) of \(\mathrm{N_2}\) at STP: \(\dfrac{28 \times 41.908}{22400} \approx 0.052385\text{ g}\). 4. \(\text{Percentage of nitrogen} = \dfrac{0.052385}{0.30} \times 100 \approx 17.46\%\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking units: \(p_1\) in \(\text{mm Hg}\), \(V\) in \(\text{mL}\), mass in \(\text{g}\). The calculated value \(17.46\%\) exactly matches the standard textbook solution. The final answer is 17.46.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_NUM_Q17 - Percentage of oxygen from carbon dioxide estimation

questiontext.text: In the direct estimation of oxygen, an organic compound is decomposed in a stream of nitrogen. The liberated oxygen is converted to \(\mathrm{CO}\) over red-hot coke and subsequently oxidised to \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) by \(\mathrm{I_2O_5}\). If \(0.20\text{ g}\) of the organic compound produces \(0.22\text{ g}\) of \(\mathrm{CO_2}\), calculate the percentage of oxygen in the compound.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of organic compound taken, \(m = 0.20\text{ g}\); mass of carbon dioxide (\(\mathrm{CO_2}\)) produced, \(m_1 = 0.22\text{ g}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
The chemical transformations are: \[2\mathrm{C} + \mathrm{O_2} \xrightarrow{1373\text{ K}} 2\mathrm{CO}\] \[\mathrm{I_2O_5} + 5\mathrm{CO} \longrightarrow \mathrm{I_2} + 5\mathrm{CO_2}\] Multiplying the first equation by 5 and the second by 2 gives: \[5\mathrm{O_2} \equiv 10\mathrm{CO} \equiv 10\mathrm{CO_2}\] Hence, \(1\text{ mol of } \mathrm{O_2}\) (\(32\text{ g}\)) produces \(2\text{ mol of } \mathrm{CO_2}\) (\(2 \times 44 = 88\text{ g}\)).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Percentage of oxygen = \(\dfrac{32 \times m_1 \times 100}{88 \times m}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substituting the given values: \[\text{Percentage of oxygen} = \frac{32 \times 0.22\text{ g} \times 100}{88 \times 0.20\text{ g}}\] Simplify algebraically: \[\frac{0.22}{88} = \frac{1}{400} = 0.0025\text{ mol of } \mathrm{O_2}\] \[\text{Mass of oxygen} = \frac{32 \times 0.22}{88} = 0.08\text{ g}\] \[\text{Percentage of oxygen} = \frac{0.08\text{ g}}{0.20\text{ g}} \times 100 = 40.0\%\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking the ratio: \(0.08 / 0.20 = 8/20 = 40.0\%\). The stoichiometry and calculations are consistent with the textbook derivation. The final answer is 40.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_NUM_Q18 - Mass of carbon dioxide from combustion percentage

questiontext.text: An organic compound contains \(69.0\%\) carbon and \(4.8\%\) hydrogen, the remainder being oxygen. Calculate the mass of carbon dioxide (in grams) produced when \(0.20\text{ g}\) of this substance is subjected to complete combustion.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of organic compound, \(m = 0.20\text{ g}\); percentage of carbon in compound = \(69.0\%\); molar mass of \(\mathrm{CO_2} = 44\text{ g mol}^{-1}\); atomic mass of carbon = \(12\text{ g mol}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
During combustion, all carbon in the sample is converted into carbon dioxide. The mass of carbon dioxide produced, \(m_2\), is directly related to the mass of carbon present.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
\(\text{Percentage of carbon} = \dfrac{12 \times m_2 \times 100}{44 \times m}\). Rearranging for \(m_2\): \[m_2 = \frac{\text{Percentage of carbon} \times 44 \times m}{12 \times 100}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substituting the given numerical values: \[m_2 = \frac{69.0 \times 44 \times 0.20\text{ g}}{1200}\] Calculate intermediate products: - Numerator: \(69.0 \times 44 \times 0.20 = 607.2\). - Division: \(m_2 = \dfrac{607.2}{1200} = 0.506\text{ g}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking the mass of carbon: \(0.20 \times 0.69 = 0.138\text{ g}\) of C. Mass of \(\mathrm{CO_2} = 0.138 \times (44/12) = 0.138 \times 3.6667 = 0.506\text{ g}\). The calculation is verified. The final answer is 0.506.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_NUM_Q19 - Phosphorus estimation via magnesium pyrophosphate precipitate

questiontext.text: In the estimation of phosphorus, \(0.31\text{ g}\) of an organic compound was oxidized to phosphoric acid and precipitated as \(\mathrm{MgNH_4PO_4}\), which on ignition yielded \(0.222\text{ g}\) of magnesium pyrophosphate (\(\mathrm{Mg_2P_2O_7}\)). Calculate the percentage of phosphorus in the compound. (Take molar mass of \(\mathrm{Mg_2P_2O_7} = 222\text{ g mol}^{-1}\), atomic mass of \(\mathrm{P} = 31\text{ u}\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of organic compound, \(m = 0.31\text{ g}\); mass of \(\mathrm{Mg_2P_2O_7}\) residue after ignition, \(m_1 = 0.222\text{ g}\); molar mass of \(\mathrm{Mg_2P_2O_7} = 222\text{ g mol}^{-1}\); mass of two phosphorus atoms = \(2 \times 31 = 62\text{ g mol}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
Each mole of magnesium pyrophosphate (\(\mathrm{Mg_2P_2O_7}\)) contains two moles of phosphorus atoms. Thus, \(222\text{ g}\) of \(\mathrm{Mg_2P_2O_7}\) contains \(62\text{ g}\) of phosphorus.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Percentage of phosphorus = \(\dfrac{62 \times m_1 \times 100}{222 \times m}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substituting the given values: \[\text{Percentage of phosphorus} = \frac{62 \times 0.222\text{ g} \times 100}{222 \times 0.31\text{ g}}\] Notice that \(\dfrac{0.222}{222} = 0.001\text{ mol}\). Mass of phosphorus in the residue = \(62 \times 0.001 = 0.062\text{ g}\). \[\text{Percentage of phosphorus} = \frac{0.062\text{ g}}{0.31\text{ g}} \times 100 = 20.0\%\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking ratio: \(0.062 / 0.31 = 62 / 310 = 1/5 = 0.20 = 20.0\%\). Result is verified. The final answer is 20.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_NUM_Q20 - Percentage of sulphur in organic Carius analysis

questiontext.text: In the estimation of sulphur by Carius method, \(0.468\text{ g}\) of an organic sulphur compound afforded \(0.668\text{ g}\) of barium sulphate. Find the percentage of sulphur in the given compound. (Take molar mass of \(\mathrm{BaSO_4} = 233\text{ g mol}^{-1}\), atomic mass of \(\mathrm{S} = 32\text{ u}\). Give answer to two decimal places).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of organic sulphur compound, \(m = 0.468\text{ g}\); mass of barium sulphate formed, \(m_1 = 0.668\text{ g}\); molar mass of \(\mathrm{BaSO_4} = 233\text{ g mol}^{-1}\); atomic mass of sulphur = \(32\text{ g mol}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
Sulphur is converted quantitatively to sulphate and precipitated as barium sulphate (\(\mathrm{BaSO_4}\)). One mole of \(\mathrm{BaSO_4}\) (\(233\text{ g}\)) contains one mole of sulphur (\(32\text{ g}\)).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Percentage of sulphur = \(\dfrac{32 \times m_1 \times 100}{233 \times m}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substituting the numerical values into the formula: \[\text{Percentage of sulphur} = \frac{32 \times 0.668\text{ g} \times 100}{233 \times 0.468\text{ g}}\] Evaluate numerator and denominator: - Numerator: \(32 \times 0.668 \times 100 = 2137.6\). - Denominator: \(233 \times 0.468 = 109.044\). - Ratio: \(\dfrac{2137.6}{109.044} \approx 19.6029\% \approx 19.60\%\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking the intermediate mass of sulphur: \(\dfrac{32 \times 0.668}{233} \approx 0.09174\text{ g}\). Fraction: \(\dfrac{0.09174}{0.468} \times 100 \approx 19.60\%\). The answer is verified to two decimal places. The final answer is 19.60.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ORGANICCHEMISTRY_SEQUENCING_Q01 - Chronological order of historical organic syntheses

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following historical milestones in the development of organic chemistry in the correct chronological order:

(A) Synthesis of methane by Berthelot
(B) Formulation of the Vital Force Theory by Berzelius
(C) Synthesis of acetic acid from constituent elements by Kolbe
(D) Synthesis of urea from an inorganic compound by Wöhler

Choose the correct sequence from the options below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Historical background and governing concept
In the early nineteenth century, organic compounds were believed to originate solely from living organisms through a mysterious supernatural power termed "vital force". Subsequent laboratory syntheses demonstrated conclusively that organic molecules obey the same physical and chemical laws as inorganic compounds.

Step 2: Chronological evaluation of each milestone
1. Berzelius proposed the Vital Force Theory in 1815, positing that a vital force was indispensable for synthesising organic compounds, corresponding to (B).
2. Friedrich Wöhler disproved the vital force theory in 1828 by heating ammonium cyanate (an inorganic salt) to yield urea (an organic compound), corresponding to (D).
3. Hermann Kolbe achieved the total synthesis of acetic acid from its constituent elements in 1845, corresponding to (C).
4. Marcellin Berthelot synthesised methane from inorganic precursors in 1856, providing final confirmation of laboratory organic synthesis, corresponding to (A).

Step 3: Determination of chronological sequence
Arranging these discoveries in advancing order of occurrence gives 1815 \(\rightarrow\) 1828 \(\rightarrow\) 1845 \(\rightarrow\) 1856.

Therefore, the correct chronological sequence is (B) \(\rightarrow\) (D) \(\rightarrow\) (C) \(\rightarrow\) (A).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ORGANICCHEMISTRY_SEQUENCING_Q02 - Increasing order of carbon orbital electronegativity

questiontext.text:
Consider carbon atoms exhibiting different states of hybridisation:

(A) \(sp^3\) hybridised carbon
(B) \(sp\) hybridised carbon
(C) \(sp^2\) hybridised carbon

Arrange these hybridised states in the increasing order of their electronegativity:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Governing principle
Electronegativity of a hybrid orbital depends directly on its fraction of \(s\)-character. Because electrons in \(s\)-orbitals are spherical, closer to the positively charged atomic nucleus, and held more tightly than electrons in \(p\)-orbitals, a hybrid orbital with a greater fraction of \(s\)-character exhibits greater effective electronegativity.

Step 2: Evaluation of \(s\)-character for each hybrid state
1. In \(sp^3\) hybridisation, the percentage of \(s\)-character is \(\frac{1}{4} \times 100\% = 25\%\), corresponding to (A).
2. In \(sp^2\) hybridisation, the percentage of \(s\)-character is \(\frac{1}{3} \times 100\% \approx 33.33\%\), corresponding to (C).
3. In \(sp\) hybridisation, the percentage of \(s\)-character is \(\frac{1}{2} \times 100\% = 50\%\), corresponding to (B).

Step 3: Determination of increasing sequence
Comparing the percentages of \(s\)-character:
\(25\% < 33.33\% < 50\%\).
Consequently, the electronegativity increases in the exact order of increasing \(s\)-character: \(sp^3 < sp^2 < sp\).

Therefore, the correct increasing sequence is (A) \(<\) (C) \(<\) (B).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ORGANICCHEMISTRY_SEQUENCING_Q03 - Sequential steps in branched alkane nomenclature

questiontext.text:
Consider the following procedural steps employed in assigning the systematic IUPAC name to a branched-chain alkane:

(A) Number the carbon atoms of the parent continuous chain from the terminus that allocates the lowest locant set to the substituent branches.
(B) Assemble the substituent prefixes alphabetically with their respective locants immediately preceding the parent alkane root name.
(C) Identify the longest continuous chain of carbon atoms to establish the parent alkane framework.
(D) Apply multiplicative prefixes (such as di-, tri-, tetra-) when identical substituent groups appear at different or identical carbon positions.

Arrange these operations in the correct logical sequence of execution:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identification of parent structure
According to IUPAC nomenclature rules, the first essential operation is to determine the longest continuous chain of carbon atoms in the molecule, which dictates the parent hydrocarbon stem, corresponding to (C).

Step 2: Numbering the parent carbon chain
Once the parent chain is chosen, the carbon atoms must be numbered consecutively from one end to the other such that the branched substituents receive the lowest possible locants according to the lowest locant rule, corresponding to (A).

Step 3: Addressing multiple identical substituents
If two or more identical substituents are attached to the main chain, multiplicative numerical prefixes such as di-, tri-, or tetra- are assigned along with all appropriate locants separated by commas, corresponding to (D).

Step 4: Assembling the complete IUPAC name
Finally, the names of the substituent groups are arranged in alphabetical order (ignoring prefixes like di-, tri-, sec-, tert-) and combined with their locants before the root name of the parent alkane to construct the final unambiguous IUPAC name, corresponding to (B).

Step 5: Synthesising the complete procedure
The necessary progression is: longest continuous chain selection \(\rightarrow\) lowest locant numbering \(\rightarrow\) assignment of multiplicative prefixes \(\rightarrow\) alphabetical assembly of prefixes before parent root.

Therefore, the correct logical sequence is (C) \(\rightarrow\) (A) \(\rightarrow\) (D) \(\rightarrow\) (B).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ORGANICCHEMISTRY_SEQUENCING_Q04 - Decreasing priority order of functional groups

questiontext.text:
Consider the following functional groups present in polyfunctional organic molecules:

(A) \(\mathrm{-CHO}\) (Aldehyde)
(B) \(\mathrm{-COOH}\) (Carboxylic acid)
(C) \(\mathrm{-OH}\) (Alcohol)
(D) \(\mathrm{-COOR}\) (Ester)

Arrange these functional groups in the decreasing order of priority for selection as the principal functional group in IUPAC nomenclature:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual basis of priority order
In IUPAC nomenclature of polyfunctional organic compounds, one principal functional group determines the principal class and suffix of the compound, while all remaining functional groups are treated as substituent prefixes. Priority is determined by the IUPAC priority table.

Step 2: Canonical IUPAC priority series
The established sequence of seniority from highest to lowest precedence among common functional groups is:
\(\mathrm{-COOH} > \mathrm{-SO_3H} > \text{acid anhydrides} > \mathrm{-COOR} > \mathrm{-COCl} > \mathrm{-CONH_2} > \mathrm{-CN} > \mathrm{-CHO} > \mathrm{>C=O} > \mathrm{-OH} > \mathrm{-NH_2} > \mathrm{>C=C<} > \mathrm{-C\equiv C-}\).

Step 3: Comparative ranking of the given groups
1. Carboxylic acid (\(\mathrm{-COOH}\)), designated as (B), occupies the highest position among organic oxygen acids.
2. Ester (\(\mathrm{-COOR}\)), designated as (D), is a carboxylic acid derivative and precedes carbonyl compounds.
3. Aldehyde (\(\mathrm{-CHO}\)), designated as (A), ranks higher than ketones and alcohols.
4. Hydroxyl group / alcohol (\(\mathrm{-OH}\)), designated as (C), ranks below carbonyl functions.

Step 4: Establishing decreasing priority
The correct sequence from highest to lowest priority is:
\(\mathrm{-COOH} > \mathrm{-COOR} > \mathrm{-CHO} > \mathrm{-OH}\).

Therefore, the correct decreasing sequence is (B) \(>\) (D) \(>\) (A) \(>\) (C).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ORGANICCHEMISTRY_SEQUENCING_Q05 - Increasing stability order of carbocations

questiontext.text:
Consider the following simple alkyl carbocations:

(A) \(\mathrm{\overset{+}{C}H_3}\) (Methyl cation)
(B) \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_3\overset{+}{C}}\) (tert-Butyl cation)
(C) \(\mathrm{CH_3\overset{+}{C}H_2}\) (Ethyl cation)
(D) \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_2\overset{+}{C}H}\) (Isopropyl cation)

Arrange these carbocations in the increasing order of their relative thermodynamic stability:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Principles governing carbocation stability
Carbocations are planar, \(sp^2\)-hybridised, electron-deficient species bearing an empty unhybridised \(p\)-orbital on the positively charged carbon atom. They are stabilised through two major electronic phenomena:
1. Hyperconjugation (\(\sigma\)-\(p\) orbital overlap) involving \(\mathrm{C-H}\) \(\sigma\)-bonds adjacent to the cationic carbon (\(\alpha\)-hydrogens). Greater number of \(\alpha\)-hydrogens provides greater hyperconjugative delocalisation of the positive charge.
2. Electron-releasing inductive effect (\(+I\) effect) of adjacent alkyl groups, which disperses positive charge density toward the cationic center.

Step 2: Counting \(\alpha\)-hydrogens for each carbocation
1. In the methyl cation \(\mathrm{\overset{+}{C}H_3}\), designated as (A), there are zero adjacent carbon atoms and hence 0 \(\alpha\)-hydrogens.
2. In the ethyl cation \(\mathrm{CH_3\overset{+}{C}H_2}\), designated as (C), there is one methyl group attached, giving 3 \(\alpha\)-hydrogens.
3. In the isopropyl cation \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_2\overset{+}{C}H}\), designated as (D), there are two methyl groups attached, giving \(2 \times 3 = 6\) \(\alpha\)-hydrogens.
4. In the tert-butyl cation \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_3\overset{+}{C}}\), designated as (B), there are three methyl groups attached, giving \(3 \times 3 = 9\) \(\alpha\)-hydrogens.

Step 3: Ranking in increasing order of stability
As the number of hyperconjugative structures increases from 0 to 3 to 6 to 9, stability increases strictly in the sequence:
\(\mathrm{\overset{+}{C}H_3} < \mathrm{CH_3\overset{+}{C}H_2} < \mathrm{(CH_3)_2\overset{+}{C}H} < \mathrm{(CH_3)_3\overset{+}{C}}\).

Therefore, the correct increasing sequence is (A) \(<\) (C) \(<\) (D) \(<\) (B).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ORGANICCHEMISTRY_SEQUENCING_Q06 - Procedural steps in Lassaigne test for nitrogen

questiontext.text:
The following procedural operations are carried out to detect the presence of nitrogen in an organic compound via Lassaigne's test:

(A) Boil the sodium fusion extract with freshly prepared iron(II) sulphate (\(\mathrm{FeSO_4}\)) solution.
(B) Heat the organic compound with sodium metal in an ignition tube, plunge the glowing tube into distilled water, boil, and filter to obtain the sodium fusion extract.
(C) Acidify the cooled mixture with concentrated sulphuric acid (\(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\)).
(D) Observe the development of a distinct Prussian blue precipitate or colouration.

Arrange these operations in the correct sequential order of execution:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Preparation of sodium fusion extract
Covalently bound nitrogen and carbon in the organic compound are first converted into ionic sodium cyanide by fusing with molten sodium metal in an ignition tube: \(\mathrm{Na + C + N \xrightarrow{\Delta} NaCN}\). The incandescent tube is plunged into distilled water, boiled, and filtered to harvest the aqueous extract, corresponding to (B).

Step 2: Formation of hexacyanidoferrate(II) complex
A portion of the sodium fusion extract is boiled with freshly prepared \(\mathrm{FeSO_4}\) solution. In the alkaline medium, \(\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}\) ions react with cyanide ions (\(\mathrm{CN^-}\)) to form sodium hexacyanidoferrate(II):
\(\mathrm{FeSO_4 + 2NaOH \rightarrow Fe(OH)_2 + Na_2SO_4}\)
\(\mathrm{6NaCN + FeSO_4 \rightarrow Na_4[Fe(CN)_6] + Na_2SO_4}\), corresponding to (A).

Step 3: Acidification and oxidation to iron(III)
Concentrated \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\) is added to the cooled reaction mixture. The acid dissolves iron hydroxides and oxidises part of the \(\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}\) to \(\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}\) ions, corresponding to (C).

Step 4: Precipitation of Prussian blue
The generated \(\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}\) ions interact with hexacyanidoferrate(II) ions to precipitate Prussian blue, iron(III) hexacyanidoferrate(II):
\(\mathrm{4Fe^{3+} + 3[Fe(CN)_6]^{4-} \xrightarrow{xH_2O} Fe_4[Fe(CN)_6]_3\cdot xH_2O}\), corresponding to (D).

Step 5: Synthesising the operational sequence
The chronological order of chemical and experimental events is: sodium fusion extraction \(\rightarrow\) boiling with \(\mathrm{FeSO_4}\) \(\rightarrow\) acidifying with concentrated \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\) \(\rightarrow\) observing Prussian blue colour.

Therefore, the correct sequential order is (B) \(\rightarrow\) (A) \(\rightarrow\) (C) \(\rightarrow\) (D).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ORGANICCHEMISTRY_SEQUENCING_Q07 - Sequential steps in Kjeldahl nitrogen estimation

questiontext.text:
The following sequential stages are carried out in the quantitative estimation of nitrogen by Kjeldahl's method:

(A) Distil the liberated ammonia gas into an absorption flask containing a known volume of standard sulphuric acid solution.
(B) Digest the weighed organic compound with concentrated \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\) in the presence of copper sulphate or potassium sulphate to convert nitrogen quantitatively into \((\mathrm{NH_4})_2\mathrm{SO_4}\).
(C) Titrate the unneutralised residual sulphuric acid with a standard sodium hydroxide solution.
(D) Connect the digestion flask to a distillation apparatus and boil with an excess of aqueous sodium hydroxide solution.

Arrange these analytical stages in the correct operational sequence:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Digestion stage
In Kjeldahl's method, the first stage involves heating the weighed organic compound with concentrated \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\) in a Kjeldahl flask. A small amount of \(\mathrm{CuSO_4}\) acts as a catalyst while \(\mathrm{K_2SO_4}\) raises the boiling point of the acid. Carbon and hydrogen are oxidised to \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) and \(\mathrm{H_2O}\), while nitrogen is quantitatively converted into ammonium sulphate \((\mathrm{NH_4})_2\mathrm{SO_4}\), corresponding to (B).

Step 2: Neutralisation and liberation of ammonia
The contents of the digestion flask are cooled, diluted with water, and transferred to a distillation apparatus. An excess of concentrated sodium hydroxide solution (\(\mathrm{NaOH}\)) is introduced to decompose the ammonium sulphate and liberate free gaseous ammonia:
\((\mathrm{NH_4})_2\mathrm{SO_4} + 2\mathrm{NaOH} \rightarrow \mathrm{Na_2SO_4} + 2\mathrm{NH_3} + 2\mathrm{H_2O}\), corresponding to (D).

Step 3: Distillation and quantitative absorption
The mixture is heated, and the liberated ammonia gas is distilled and quantitatively absorbed in a measured, known excess volume of standard \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\) of known molarity:
\(2\mathrm{NH_3} + \mathrm{H_2SO_4} \rightarrow (\mathrm{NH_4})_2\mathrm{SO_4}\), corresponding to (A).

Step 4: Back-titration of residual acid
The unused, excess sulphuric acid remaining after reaction with ammonia is back-titrated against a standard solution of \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) using methyl orange or phenolphthalein indicator. The difference gives the volume of acid consumed by ammonia, enabling calculation of nitrogen percentage, corresponding to (C).

Step 5: Summary of sequential execution
The analytical workflow is strictly: acid digestion \(\rightarrow\) alkalisation \(\rightarrow\) ammonia distillation and absorption \(\rightarrow\) back-titration.

Therefore, the correct sequential order of stages is (B) \(\rightarrow\) (D) \(\rightarrow\) (A) \(\rightarrow\) (C).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ORGANICCHEMISTRY_SEQUENCING_Q08 - Sequential steps in Carius sulphur estimation

questiontext.text:
Consider the following laboratory stages involved in the quantitative estimation of sulphur present in an organic compound by the Carius method:

(A) Add an excess of aqueous barium chloride (\(\mathrm{BaCl_2}\)) solution to precipitate insoluble barium sulphate.
(B) Heat a known mass of the organic compound with fuming nitric acid (\(\mathrm{HNO_3}\)) in a sealed hard-glass Carius tube inside an iron jacket.
(C) Filter, thoroughly wash, dry, and ignite the collected precipitate to obtain a constant mass.
(D) Complete the oxidative cleavage of organic sulphur into sulphuric acid (\(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\)).

Arrange these operations in the correct chronological and analytical sequence:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Sealed tube heating (Carius digestion)
A precisely weighed mass of the organic compound is introduced into a clean, dry Carius tube containing fuming nitric acid. The tube is hermetically sealed and heated in a furnace at elevated temperatures (\(\sim 550\text{--}600\text{ K}\)) inside an iron protective jacket, corresponding to (B).

Step 2: Chemical oxidation to sulphuric acid
During prolonged heating in the sealed system, fuming nitric acid completely oxidises the organic matrix. The carbon is oxidised to \(\mathrm{CO_2}\), hydrogen to \(\mathrm{H_2O}\), and the covalently bonded sulphur is quantitatively oxidised to sulphuric acid (\(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\)):
\(\mathrm{S + 2HNO_3 \xrightarrow{\Delta} H_2SO_4 + 2NO}\), corresponding to (D).

Step 3: Precipitation of barium sulphate
After cooling, the tube is safely opened, and the reaction mixture is rinsed thoroughly with distilled water into a beaker. An excess of aqueous \(\mathrm{BaCl_2}\) solution is added to the warm solution to precipitate all sulphate ions quantitatively as insoluble barium sulphate:
\(\mathrm{H_2SO_4 + BaCl_2 \rightarrow BaSO_4\downarrow + 2HCl}\), corresponding to (A).

Step 4: Gravimetric isolation and quantification
The white precipitate of \(\mathrm{BaSO_4}\) is filtered through an ashless filter paper or a Gooch crucible, washed free of chloride ions with hot water, dried, and ignited in a crucible to obtain pure anhydrous \(\mathrm{BaSO_4}\) at constant mass, from which the percentage of sulphur is calculated, corresponding to (C).

Step 5: Logical progression of analytical stages
The necessary sequence is: heating in sealed tube \(\rightarrow\) oxidation of sulphur to sulphuric acid \(\rightarrow\) precipitation with \(\mathrm{BaCl_2}\) \(\rightarrow\) filtration, ignition, and weighing of \(\mathrm{BaSO_4}\).

Therefore, the correct chronological and analytical sequence is (B) \(\rightarrow\) (D) \(\rightarrow\) (A) \(\rightarrow\) (C).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_SOME_BASIC_PRINCIPLES_AND_TECHNIQUES_MCQ_Q01 - Synthesis of urea from inorganic compound

questiontext.text: The 'vital force theory' proposing that a mysterious vital force was responsible for the formation of organic compounds was disproved in 1828 by Friedrich Wöhler through the synthesis of which organic compound from ammonium cyanate?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the historical context and reactant
In 1828, Friedrich Wöhler heated ammonium cyanate, an inorganic compound with the chemical formula \(\mathrm{NH}_4\mathrm{CNO}\).

Step 2: Determine the product formed
Upon heating, ammonium cyanate rearranged to form urea, \(\mathrm{NH}_2\mathrm{CONH}_2\), which is an organic compound found in urine.

Step 3: Verify against vital force theory
The laboratory synthesis of an organic compound from an inorganic precursor conclusively rejected Berzelius's vital force theory.

Therefore, the correct answer is Urea.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_SOME_BASIC_PRINCIPLES_AND_TECHNIQUES_MCQ_Q02 - Pioneering laboratory synthesis of acetic acid

questiontext.text: The pioneering synthesis of acetic acid from inorganic sources in the laboratory was achieved in 1845 by which chemist?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Review the historical development of organic synthesis
Following Wöhler's synthesis of urea in 1828, chemists demonstrated that other organic molecules could be synthesised from elemental or inorganic sources.

Step 2: Identify the specific scientist and year
Kolbe in 1845 achieved the synthesis of acetic acid, and Berthelot later synthesised methane in 1856.

Step 3: Formulate the final conclusion
The laboratory synthesis of acetic acid from its constituent elements in 1845 was accomplished by Kolbe.

Therefore, the correct answer is Kolbe.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_SOME_BASIC_PRINCIPLES_AND_TECHNIQUES_MCQ_Q03 - Electronegativity trend of hybridised carbon atoms

questiontext.text: Which of the following correctly represents the decreasing order of electronegativity of carbon atoms based on their hybridisation state?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Relate hybridisation to s-character
An \(sp\) hybrid orbital has \(50\%\) \(s\)-character, an \(sp^2\) hybrid orbital has \(33.3\%\) \(s\)-character, and an \(sp^3\) hybrid orbital has \(25\%\) \(s\)-character.

Step 2: Analyze the relationship between s-character and electronegativity
Orbitals with greater \(s\)-character are closer to the atomic nucleus and experience greater effective nuclear attraction, resulting in higher electronegativity.

Step 3: Establish the decreasing order
Because electronegativity increases with increasing \(s\)-character, the decreasing order is \(sp > sp^2 > sp^3\).

Therefore, the correct answer is \(sp > sp^2 > sp^3\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_SOME_BASIC_PRINCIPLES_AND_TECHNIQUES_MCQ_Q04 - Reason for restricted rotation about carbon double bond

questiontext.text: Rotation about a carbon-carbon double bond (\(\mathrm{C=C}\)) in ethene is restricted primarily because:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Understand the orbital overlap required for pi bond formation
A \(\pi\) bond forms through the sideways (lateral) overlap of two unhybridised \(p\) orbitals that are parallel to each other and perpendicular to the molecular plane.

Step 2: Evaluate the effect of fragment rotation
Rotating one \(\mathrm{CH}_2\) group relative to the other tilts the \(p\) orbitals out of parallel alignment, breaking or diminishing the maximum sideways overlap of the \(p\) orbitals.

Step 3: State the physical consequence
Because destroying this orbital overlap requires substantial energy, free rotation about the double bond is restricted.

Therefore, the correct answer is rotation disrupts the parallel alignment and maximum overlap of the unhybridised \(p\) orbitals.

answer.text: the \(\sigma\) bond between the two carbon atoms is broken upon rotation
the hydrogen atoms experience excessive steric clash across the double bond
the \(sp^2\) hybrid orbitals undergo rehybridisation to \(sp^3\) during rotation
rotation disrupts the parallel alignment and maximum overlap of the unhybridised \(p\) orbitals

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_SOME_BASIC_PRINCIPLES_AND_TECHNIQUES_MCQ_Q05 - Location and reactivity of pi electron cloud

questiontext.text: In a molecule containing a carbon-carbon double bond, the \(\pi\)-electron charge cloud is located:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Describe the geometry of pi bonding
The \(\sigma\) bond framework lies in the molecular plane, formed by head-on overlap along the internuclear axis.

Step 2: Determine the spatial distribution of pi electrons
The \(\pi\) bond is formed by lateral overlap of parallel \(p\) orbitals oriented perpendicular to the molecular plane, positioning the electron density directly above and below the plane of the bonding atoms.

Step 3: Relate to reactivity
Because the \(\pi\) electrons reside exposed above and below the plane, they are easily accessible to attacking electrophilic reagents.

Therefore, the correct answer is above and below the plane of the bonding atoms.

answer.text: above and below the plane of the bonding atoms
strictly along the internuclear axis between the carbon atoms
in a spherically symmetric sphere surrounding both carbon nuclei

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_SOME_BASIC_PRINCIPLES_AND_TECHNIQUES_MCQ_Q06 - Sigma and pi bonds in pentenyme hydrocarbon

questiontext.text: How many total \(\sigma\) and \(\pi\) bonds are present in the molecule \(\mathrm{HC}\equiv\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_3\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Count carbon-hydrogen sigma bonds
There is 1 \(\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{H}\) bond at \(\mathrm{C}_1\), 1 at \(\mathrm{C}_3\), 1 at \(\mathrm{C}_4\), and 3 at \(\mathrm{C}_5\), giving \(1 + 1 + 1 + 3 = 6\) \(\sigma_{\mathrm{C-H}}\) bonds.

Step 2: Count carbon-carbon sigma and pi bonds
Between \(\mathrm{C}_1\) and \(\mathrm{C}_2\) (triple bond), there is 1 \(\sigma\) and 2 \(\pi\) bonds. Between \(\mathrm{C}_2\) and \(\mathrm{C}_3\), there is 1 \(\sigma\) bond. Between \(\mathrm{C}_3\) and \(\mathrm{C}_4\) (double bond), there is 1 \(\sigma\) and 1 \(\pi\) bond. Between \(\mathrm{C}_4\) and \(\mathrm{C}_5\), there is 1 \(\sigma\) bond. Total \(\sigma_{\mathrm{C-C}} = 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 4\).

Step 3: Calculate total sigma and pi bonds
Total \(\sigma = 6 + 4 = 10\) \(\sigma\) bonds. Total \(\pi = 2 + 1 = 3\) \(\pi\) bonds.

Therefore, the correct answer is \(10\,\sigma\) and \(3\,\pi\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_SOME_BASIC_PRINCIPLES_AND_TECHNIQUES_MCQ_Q07 - Count of sigma and pi bonds in buta-1,2-diene

questiontext.text: What is the total number of \(\sigma\) and \(\pi\) bonds in the allene derivative \(\mathrm{CH}_2=\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_3\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Count carbon-hydrogen sigma bonds
There are 2 hydrogens on \(\mathrm{C}_1\), none on \(\mathrm{C}_2\), 1 on \(\mathrm{C}_3\), and 3 on \(\mathrm{C}_4\), giving \(2 + 0 + 1 + 3 = 6\) \(\sigma_{\mathrm{C-H}}\) bonds.

Step 2: Count carbon-carbon sigma and pi bonds
The backbone consists of two contiguous double bonds and one single bond: \(\mathrm{C}_1=\mathrm{C}_2\) has 1 \(\sigma\) and 1 \(\pi\); \(\mathrm{C}_2=\mathrm{C}_3\) has 1 \(\sigma\) and 1 \(\pi\); \(\mathrm{C}_3-\mathrm{C}_4\) has 1 \(\sigma\). Total \(\sigma_{\mathrm{C-C}} = 3\), total \(\pi = 2\).

Step 3: Calculate sum of bonds
Total \(\sigma\) bonds \(= 6 + 3 = 9\), and total \(\pi\) bonds \(= 2\).

Therefore, the correct answer is \(9\,\sigma\) and \(2\,\pi\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_SOME_BASIC_PRINCIPLES_AND_TECHNIQUES_MCQ_Q08 - Hybridisation states of carbons in but-2-enenitrile

questiontext.text: In the molecule \(\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CN}\), what are the hybridisation states of the carbon atoms from left to right?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analyze each carbon atom sequentially
Carbon 1 (methyl carbon): bonded to three hydrogens and one carbon by single bonds, with 4 \(\sigma\) bonds and no lone pairs, so it is \(sp^3\) hybridised.

Step 2: Evaluate double-bonded carbons
Carbon 2 and Carbon 3 are each involved in a carbon-carbon double bond, possessing 3 \(\sigma\) bonds and 1 \(\pi\) bond each, making them \(sp^2\) hybridised.

Step 3: Evaluate the nitrile carbon
The nitrile carbon is bonded to one carbon via a single bond and to nitrogen via a triple bond (\(\mathrm{C}\equiv\mathrm{N}\)), possessing 2 \(\sigma\) bonds and 2 \(\pi\) bonds, making it \(sp\) hybridised.

Step 4: Combine from left to right
The sequence of hybridisation is \(sp^3\), \(sp^2\), \(sp^2\), \(sp\).

Therefore, the correct answer is \(sp^3, sp^2, sp^2, sp\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_SOME_BASIC_PRINCIPLES_AND_TECHNIQUES_MCQ_Q09 - Hybrid orbitals forming specific carbon-carbon bond

questiontext.text: In the hydrocarbon \(\overset{6}{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{H}_2=\overset{5}{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{H}-\overset{4}{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{H}_2-\\overset{3}{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{H}_2-\overset{2}{\mathrm{C}}\equiv\overset{1}{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{H}\), according to IUPAC numbering (numbering from the alkyne end because both triple and double bonds are at terminal positions but double bond gets lower locant or vice versa), what is the pair of hybridised orbitals involved in the formation of the \(\mathrm{C}_2-\mathrm{C}_3\) bond?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Determine IUPAC numbering of the chain
The chain contains 6 carbons with a double bond and a triple bond at terminal positions (1 and 5). By IUPAC priority when double and triple bonds are equidistant from ends, the double bond receives the lower locant (carbon-1). Thus: \(\overset{1}{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{H}_2=\overset{2}{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{H}-\overset{3}{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{H}_2-\overset{4}{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{H}_2-\overset{5}{\mathrm{C}}\equiv\overset{6}{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{H}\).

Step 2: Determine hybridisation of C2 and C3
Carbon-2 has a double bond (\(\mathrm{C}_1=\mathrm{C}_2\)) and two single bonds, so it has 3 \(\sigma\) bonds and is \(sp^2\) hybridised. Carbon-3 has single bonds to \(\mathrm{C}_2\), \(\mathrm{C}_4\), and two hydrogens, giving 4 \(\sigma\) bonds, so it is \(sp^3\) hybridised.

Step 3: Conclude the orbital overlap for C2-C3 bond
The \(\sigma\) bond between \(\mathrm{C}_2\) and \(\mathrm{C}_3\) is formed by the overlap of an \(sp^2\) orbital from \(\mathrm{C}_2\) and an \(sp^3\) orbital from \(\mathrm{C}_3\).

Therefore, the correct answer is \(sp^2 - sp^3\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_SOME_BASIC_PRINCIPLES_AND_TECHNIQUES_MCQ_Q10 - Hybridisation and geometry of formaldehyde and hydrogen cyanide

questiontext.text: What are the state of hybridisation of the carbon atom and the molecular shape for methanal (\(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O}\)) and hydrogen cyanide (\(\mathrm{HCN}\)), respectively?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analyze methanal (H2C=O)
The central carbon atom forms two \(\sigma\) bonds to hydrogen and one \(\sigma\) plus one \(\pi\) bond to oxygen. With 3 \(\sigma\) bonds and zero lone pairs, the steric number is 3, corresponding to \(sp^2\) hybridisation and a trigonal planar geometry.

Step 2: Analyze hydrogen cyanide (HCN)
The central carbon atom forms one \(\sigma\) bond to hydrogen and one \(\sigma\) plus two \(\pi\) bonds to nitrogen. With 2 \(\sigma\) bonds and zero lone pairs, the steric number is 2, corresponding to \(sp\) hybridisation and a linear geometry.

Step 3: Combine both results
Methanal has an \(sp^2\) hybridised carbon with trigonal planar shape, while hydrogen cyanide has an \(sp\) hybridised carbon with linear shape.

Therefore, the correct answer is \(sp^2\), trigonal planar and \(sp\), linear.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_SOME_BASIC_PRINCIPLES_AND_TECHNIQUES_MCQ_Q11 - Three dimensional representation conventions on paper

questiontext.text: In the three-dimensional wedge-and-dash representation of an organic molecule on paper, which symbol denotes a bond projecting out of the plane of paper towards the observer?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Review the standard conventions of wedge-and-dash formulas
Normal lines (—) depict bonds lying in the plane of the paper.

Step 2: Differentiate between solid and dashed wedges
The dashed wedge (\(\dots\)) depicts a bond projecting into the paper, away from the observer. The solid wedge (—) depicts a bond projecting out of the plane of the paper, towards the observer.

Step 3: Identify the correct notation
The bond directed towards the observer is represented by a solid wedge.

Therefore, the correct answer is A solid wedge.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_SOME_BASIC_PRINCIPLES_AND_TECHNIQUES_MCQ_Q12 - Characteristics of space filling molecular model

questiontext.text: Which type of molecular model emphasizes the relative size of each atom based on its van der Waals radius without showing explicit bond sticks?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Examine the three common types of molecular models
Framework models show only the bonds connecting atoms, ball-and-stick models show both atoms and bonds, and space-filling models represent atoms as spheres without showing bonds.

Step 2: Analyze the space-filling model
The space-filling model uses spheres proportional to the van der Waals radii of atoms to convey the volume occupied by each atom in the molecule.

Step 3: Conclude the matching model
The model emphasizing the relative atomic size based on van der Waals radii is the space-filling model.

Therefore, the correct answer is Space-filling model.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_SOME_BASIC_PRINCIPLES_AND_TECHNIQUES_MCQ_Q13 - Classification of tetrahydrofuran as heterocyclic alicyclic

questiontext.text: Tetrahydrofuran (THF) is classified as which type of organic compound according to structural classification?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the structure of tetrahydrofuran
Tetrahydrofuran is a five-membered saturated ring consisting of four carbon atoms and one oxygen atom.

Step 2: Evaluate ring characteristics
Because it contains a ring of atoms containing an element other than carbon (oxygen), it is heterocyclic.

Step 3: Evaluate aromaticity
It contains only single bonds and behaves like an aliphatic ether rather than an aromatic compound, making it an alicyclic heterocyclic compound.

Therefore, the correct answer is Alicyclic heterocyclic compound.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_SOME_BASIC_PRINCIPLES_AND_TECHNIQUES_MCQ_Q14 - Identification of non-benzenoid aromatic compound

questiontext.text: Which of the following compounds is an example of a non-benzenoid aromatic compound as described in the classification of organic compounds?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Define non-benzenoid aromatic compounds
Non-benzenoid aromatic compounds possess aromatic character and conjugated cyclic \(\pi\) systems but lack a benzene ring.

Step 2: Examine the given compounds
Benzene, aniline, and naphthalene are benzenoid aromatic compounds because they contain one or more benzene rings. Tropone (cyclohepta-2,4,6-trien-1-one) is a seven-membered aromatic ring with no benzene ring.

Step 3: Conclude the correct compound
Tropone is classified as a non-benzenoid aromatic compound.

Therefore, the correct answer is Tropone.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_SOME_BASIC_PRINCIPLES_AND_TECHNIQUES_MCQ_Q15 - Examples of heterocyclic aromatic compounds

questiontext.text: Which of the following sets consists exclusively of heterocyclic aromatic compounds?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Understand the definition of heterocyclic aromatic compounds
These are cyclic aromatic compounds containing one or more heteroatoms (such as nitrogen, oxygen, or sulphur) within the ring skeleton.

Step 2: Evaluate individual compounds
Furan contains an oxygen heteroatom in an aromatic five-membered ring; thiophene contains a sulphur heteroatom; pyridine contains a nitrogen heteroatom in a six-membered aromatic ring.

Step 3: Check the other candidates
